title: Understanding Unbiased Estimators
text: An estimator is unbiased if its expected value equals the parameter it estimates. In this case, we need to show that the expected value of \( \hat{\delta} \) equals \( \delta \).

title: Breaking Down the Estimator
text: The estimator \( \hat{\delta} \) is defined as \( \bar{K}-\bar{D} \). We need to find the expected value of this expression.

title: Using Linearity of Expectation
text: The expectation of a difference is the difference of the expectations. Therefore, \( E[\hat{\delta}] $$=$$ E[\bar{K}] - E[\bar{D}] \).

title: Substituting Known Values
text: We know that \( \bar{K} \) is an unbiased estimator of \( \mu_K \) and \( \bar{D} \) is an unbiased estimator of \( \mu_D \). Therefore, \( E[\bar{K}] $$=$$ \mu_K \) and \( E[\bar{D}] $$=$$ \mu_D \).

title: Final Calculation
text: Substitute the known expectations into the expression for \( E[\hat{\delta}] \).
